answer.rationale:
The 18% mandate plus the incumbent's refusal to reopen price makes negotiate_terms (memory_c4) unlikely to deliver this cycle, and defer_decision borrows from memory_c5, which described a NON-critical service that continued month-to-month 
o expiring 14-day primary contract on a line at 94% of committed volume is a different risk class. Straight renewal (memory_c1, memory_c6) protects delivery but concedes the cost objective outright. That leaves the low-cost vendor as the only real cost lever, and memory_c2 is the single piece of evidence for it \.: it praests onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy 
 hygiene metrics 
 and is conspicuously silent on defect rates, on-time delivery, and behavior at committed volume. That silence is exactly the dimension that matters here, so memory_c2 is the one record worth the verification budget. My intent is add_second_source, qualifying the low-cost vendor on a guarded slice while incumbent volume continues, which is the pattern memory_c3 supports (dual-sourcing held allocation through a shortage) and which builds a cost path without betting the line on an unverified reliability record. Scale is deliberately small: with no buffer, a failed qualification must not touch committed volume. Explicit caveats: (1) I am not treating memory_c2's cost win as evidence of quality or delivery performance 
 if the archive shows the cost cut came with slipped lead times or accepted defect rates, the second source cannot carry meaningful volume and this becomes a renew-and-requalify cycle; (2) this decision does not by itself resolve the expiring contract, so continuity terms with the incumbent must be secured as part of executing it or delivery risk rises rather than falls; (3) chasing an 18% cut on industrial hardware creates real pressure to relax inspection or tolerance standards downstream 
 cost gains booked that way are borrowed against field failures, and qualification gates should be held fixed regardless of the spend target; (4) one cycle of qualification data will not settle whether the low-cost vendor can hold committed volume, and I do not expect it to.
